questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. The ulcer has clean-cut edges and an indurated base. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. Which treatment is most appropriate?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. This remains the gold standard treatment for all stages of syphilis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing and erythematous skin. Nikolsky sign is negative. Biopsy shows subepidermal bulla with eosinophils. DIF reveals linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, subepidermal blistering with eosinophils, and linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF. The target antigen is BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with crusted lesions on the face and exposed extremities. He reports honey-colored crusts initially. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus. This clinical picture is most consistent with:
questions.exp: Non-bullous (crusted) impetigo is the most common form, presents with honey-colored crusts on exposed areas, caused by Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes. Ecthyma is a deeper ulcerative form.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) presents with painless white plaques on the lateral border of the tongue that cannot be scraped off. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Oral hairy leukoplakia, caused by EBV reactivation, presents as white corrugated plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off. It is an AIDS-defining condition seen with low CD4 counts. Oral candidiasis plaques can be scraped off.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk, thickened nerves, and acid-fast bacilli on slit-skin smear (BI 3+). The lepromin test is negative. What type of leprosy does this represent?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) has negative lepromin test, high bacterial index (BI 4-6+), multiple lesions with ill-defined borders, symmetrical distribution, and widespread nerve involvement. BI of 3+ indicates multibacillary disease favoring LL or BL.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with history of Raynaud's phenomenon develops tight, shiny skin on her fingers, face and chest, with salt and pepper pigmentation and telangiectasias. ANA is positive with anticentromere antibody. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Limited systemic sclerosis (CREST) is characterized by Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia. Anticentromere antibody is specific for limited SSc. Diffuse SSc has anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I).

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the elbows, knees, and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. Which histological finding is pathognomonic of this condition?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in the stratum corneum) are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses are seen in mycosis fungoides. Civatte bodies are seen in lichen planus. Acanthosis, parakeratosis, and elongated rete ridges are also seen.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with vesicular lesions in a dermatomal distribution on the right thorax, preceded by pain and burning sensation for 3 days. The most appropriate treatment within 72 hours is:
opts: Valacyclovir 1000 mg thrice daily for 7 days
Famciclovir 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster (shingles) is treated with Valacyclovir 1000 mg TDS for 7 days. It has better bioavailability than acyclovir and simpler dosing. Standard acyclovir for zoster is 800 mg 5 times/day (not 200 mg). Topical treatment alone is inadequate.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male presents with painful erythematous macules on the lower extremities that evolve into ulcers with undermined edges and necrotic base. Blood culture is positive for Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Ecthyma gangrenosum is a cutaneous manifestation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia. It starts as erythematous macules/nodules and rapidly progresses to ulcers with hemorrhagic and gangrenous centers, most commonly in immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer develops a painless papule on the hand that ulcerates and forms a black eschar surrounded by significant non-pitting edema. No fever or systemic toxicity. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax (malignant pustule) caused by Bacillus anthracis presents as a painless ulcer with a black eschar (anthrax = coal/black) surrounded by massive non-pitting edema. The hallmark is painlessness despite severe local reaction.

questions.q: A 30-year-old immunocompetent patient presents with a kerion on the scalp — a painful, boggy, purulent mass with broken hairs. KOH preparation shows endothrix pattern. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Trichophyton tonsurans causes endothrix tinea capitis (black dot type) and can cause kerion in inflammatory hosts. Microsporum causes ectothrix. T. rubrum mainly causes tinea pedis/unguium. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 55-year-old immunosuppressed patient develops painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the V1 distribution of the trigeminal nerve, with vesicles on the tip of the nose. This nasal involvement predicts:
opts: Hutchinson sign — high risk for ocular involvement
questions.exp: Hutchinson sign is vesicles on the tip of the nose (nasociliary nerve involvement), indicating the virus has spread to the nasociliary branch of V1, predicting high risk of ocular complications (herpes zoster ophthalmicus). Ramsay Hunt involves geniculate ganglion with ear vesicles.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with pruritic papules and burrows in the web spaces, wrists, and genitalia. His wife has similar symptoms. First-line treatment is:
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is the first-line treatment for scabies — most effective, safe, applied from neck down and washed off after 8-14 hours. Lindane is second-line due to neurotoxicity. Oral ivermectin is used for crusted scabies or when topical treatment fails.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with malar erythema, discoid lupus lesions, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous). The most specific antibody for this condition is:
questions.exp: Anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibody is the most specific for SLE (specificity ~99%), though sensitivity is low (25%). Anti-dsDNA is highly specific but also elevated in active disease. Anti-Ro is associated with neonatal lupus and subacute cutaneous LE. Anti-histone is associated with drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash, shawl sign, and proximal muscle weakness. CK is elevated. The characteristic nail fold finding in this condition is:
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis shows periungual telangiectasias and ragged, overgrown cuticles (Samitz sign). Gottron's papules (dorsal knuckles), heliotrope rash, shawl sign, V-sign are cutaneous features. CK elevation indicates muscle involvement.

questions.q: A neonate develops flaccid bullae at birth. Nikolsky sign is positive. Skin biopsy shows acantholysis at the suprabasal level. The mother had lesions in the third trimester. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Neonatal pemphigus occurs due to passive transfer of maternal anti-desmoglein IgG antibodies across the placenta. It resolves spontaneously within weeks as maternal antibodies are cleared. Suprabasal acantholysis and positive Nikolsky confirm pemphigus.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with a painless non-healing ulcer at the mucocutaneous junction of the mouth for 6 months. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The most important predisposing factor in Indian patients is:
questions.exp: Oral squamous cell carcinoma in India is predominantly caused by tobacco and areca nut (betel quid) chewing habits, which cause submucous fibrosis and leukoplakia as precursor lesions. This is distinct from oropharyngeal SCC where HPV (especially HPV-16) plays a major role in Western countries.

questions.q: A 65-year-old fair-skinned male presents with a pearly nodule with telangiectasias on the nose that has ulcerated centrally (rodent ulcer). Biopsy confirms basal cell carcinoma. What is the preferred treatment modality for this lesion?
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery is the preferred treatment for BCC on the nose (high-risk area, H-zone of face) due to its tissue-sparing approach and high cure rate (99%). It allows real-time margin assessment, crucial for cosmetically sensitive and functionally critical areas.

questions.q: A patient is started on dapsone for leprosy. After 2 weeks, they develop hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia. Which enzyme deficiency makes patients particularly susceptible to this adverse effect?
questions.exp: G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency makes patients highly susceptible to dapsone-induced hemolytic anemia, as G6PD is essential for protecting RBCs from oxidative stress. G6PD levels should be checked before starting dapsone. Hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia are dose-dependent side effects of dapsone.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on long-term tetracycline for acne develops phototoxic reactions. Which of the following antibiotics has the highest risk of phototoxicity?
questions.exp: Doxycycline has the highest phototoxic potential among tetracyclines. Minocycline has the least phototoxicity but is associated with drug-induced pigmentation (blue-grey discoloration), lupus-like reactions, and drug hypersensitivity syndrome. Patients on doxycycline should use sunscreen and avoid sun exposure.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with Fitzpatrick skin type IV presents for laser hair removal. Which laser is most suitable to minimize the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation?
questions.exp: Nd:YAG (1064 nm) laser is preferred for darker skin types (Fitzpatrick IV-VI) for hair removal because the longer wavelength is less absorbed by melanin in the epidermis, reducing the risk of epidermal damage and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Ruby and alexandrite lasers have more melanin absorption, making them suitable only for lighter skin types.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with discrete, flesh-colored papules on the genitals with a central umbilication. The lesions are soft and can be expressed to show white caseous material. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a poxvirus. It presents with pearly, umbilicated papules containing molluscum bodies (Henderson-Patterson bodies on histology). Genital distribution in adults suggests sexual transmission. HPV causes condylomata acuminata (cauliflower-like warts).

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with alopecia in a band-like pattern at the frontoparietal region, with perifollicular erythema, scaling, and follicular plugging. Dermoscopy shows peripilar casts and loss of follicular ostia. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA) is a form of lichen planopilaris presenting as a band-like recession of the frontoparietal hairline in postmenopausal women, though it can occur in men. Features include peripilar erythema, scaling, follicular plugging, and loss of follicular ostia — indicating irreversible scarring alopecia.

questions.q: A 35-year-old with vitiligo attends clinic. Wood's lamp examination shows chalky-white fluorescence that becomes more pronounced under the lamp. What does this indicate?
opts: Ash leaf macule of tuberous sclerosis
questions.exp: Wood's lamp (365 nm UV) examination in vitiligo shows enhanced chalk-white or bright fluorescence compared to surrounding skin, confirming complete melanocyte loss. This enhancement is most useful in fair-skinned individuals. Ash leaf macules show dull white fluorescence, while post-inflammatory hypopigmentation doesn't enhance as dramatically.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 50 cells/μL) develops disseminated skin lesions — papules, nodules, and plaques of varying morphology all over the body, including oral mucosa. Some lesions are violaceous and painless. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) in HIV/AIDS is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV) and presents as violaceous, painless papules, plaques, and nodules on skin, mucosa, and viscera. It is an AIDS-defining illness seen with CD4 <200. Bacillary angiomatosis (Bartonella) can mimic KS but is bacterial and responds to antibiotics.

questions.q: A patient develops painful, burning papulovesicular eruption in a symmetrical distribution over the buttocks and extensor surfaces. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillary tips. This patient likely has:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is characterized by intensely pruritic/burning vesicles on extensor surfaces and buttocks, with granular IgA at dermal papilla tips on DIF. It is associated with celiac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy). Treatment includes dapsone and gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male with chronic sun exposure presents with a rough, scaly patch on the right cheek and forehead. Biopsy shows full-thickness keratinocyte dysplasia with preservation of the basal layer. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Actinic keratosis (solar keratosis) shows partial-thickness epidermal dysplasia (lower layers preserved). Bowen's disease (SCC in-situ) shows full-thickness keratinocyte atypia involving the entire epidermis. Both are precancerous; treatment options include cryotherapy, 5-FU, imiquimod, or PDT.

questions.q: A Type 1 lepra reaction occurs in a patient on multidrug therapy for borderline lepromatous leprosy. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate management?
opts: Continue MDT and add prednisolone 40-60 mg/day
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reactions require continuing MDT and adding systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 40-60 mg/day tapering over 3-6 months). Stopping MDT is contraindicated as it can worsen leprosy. Thalidomide is used for Type 2 (ENL) reactions, not Type 1.

questions.q: A 20-year-old female presents with diffuse non-scarring alopecia, telogen effluvium 3 months after childbirth. The most appropriate investigation to confirm diagnosis and exclude secondary causes is:
opts: Thyroid function tests, complete blood count, ferritin
questions.exp: Postpartum telogen effluvium is common 2-4 months after delivery. While the clinical diagnosis is usually straightforward, baseline investigations including TFTs, CBC, and ferritin are essential to exclude hypothyroidism, anemia, and iron deficiency as contributing factors. Iron deficiency is especially relevant in postpartum women.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with painful reddish-brown nodules on the shins bilaterally, slightly raised above the skin surface, tender on palpation, occurring over 2 weeks. No ulceration. Associated with mild fever and arthralgia. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum presents as painful, tender, erythematous nodules on the anterior shins (pre-tibial area), without ulceration. It is a septal panniculitis and may be associated with streptococcal infection, sarcoidosis, IBD, drugs, or TB. Nodular vasculitis (erythema induratum) occurs on the calf/posterior shin and may ulcerate.

questions.q: A patient with plaque psoriasis is started on methotrexate. After 6 months, they develop fatigue, nausea, and elevated LFTs. To monitor for methotrexate-induced hepatotoxicity, the GOLD STANDARD investigation is:
opts: Procollagen-III amino terminal peptide (P-III-NP) serum levels
questions.exp: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for assessing methotrexate-induced hepatotoxicity/fibrosis. It is recommended after a cumulative dose of 1-1.5 g in patients without other risk factors. Serum LFTs are unreliable as they can be normal despite significant fibrosis. P-III-NP and FibroScan are emerging non-invasive alternatives but not yet the gold standard.
